survey.architecture: Requests is a human-friendly Python HTTP client library. It provides a high-level interface for making HTTP requests with automatic session management, cookie persistence, connection pooling, and flexible configuration. The architecture separates concerns into three main layers: a user-facing API that exposes convenience functions, a Session object that manages persistent settings across requests, and transport adapters that delegate to urllib3 for low-level HTTP mechanics. Requests also handles cross-cutting concerns like authentication, cookie handling, redirect following, and response parsing.

entry_points.what_it_starts: A new HTTP request to a remote server, creating and managing a temporary session for the request lifecycle.
A GET request by delegating to the request() function with method='get'.
A POST request by delegating to the request() function with method='post'.
A PUT request by delegating to the request() function with method='put'.
A PATCH request by delegating to the request() function with method='patch'.
A DELETE request by delegating to the request() function with method='delete'.
A HEAD request by delegating to the request() function with method='head'.
An OPTIONS request by delegating to the request() function with method='options'.
A persistent HTTP session with retained cookies, authentication, and connection pooling across multiple requests.

core_abstractions.role: User-facing request builder that collects all HTTP request parameters (method, URL, headers, body, auth, cookies, etc.) before preparation and transmission.
Immutable prepared request containing the exact bytes to be sent: normalized URL, assembled headers, encoded body, and serialized cookies.
HTTP response object with status code, headers, content, and lazy-loading properties; wraps urllib3's raw response for high-level access.
Stateful session manager that persists cookies, authentication, proxies, headers, and connection pooling across multiple requests.
Transport adapter that bridges Request/Response to urllib3, managing connection pools, SSL/TLS configuration, and exception translation.

relationships.note: Each API function creates a temporary Session context to send the request.
Session.request builds a Request object from the caller's parameters.
Session.request delegates to prepare_request to finalize the request with session defaults.
prepare_request creates and populates a PreparedRequest with merged session/request settings.
Session.request calls send to transmit the prepared request and handle responses.
Session.send retrieves an appropriate adapter via get_adapter and delegates transmission to it.
HTTPAdapter.send builds a Response from urllib3's raw response via build_response.
Session.send delegates redirect handling to resolve_redirects if allow_redirects=True.
PreparedRequest.prepare_auth applies the auth handler (which implements __call__) to add credentials.
PreparedRequest.prepare_cookies merges cookies into the request from a RequestsCookieJar.
Session maintains a RequestsCookieJar for persistent cookie storage across requests.
Session.send dispatches response hooks to allow custom processing of responses.
HTTPAdapter.send wraps urllib3 exceptions into Requests exception hierarchy.

flows.name: Simple GET request via module-level API

steps.what_happens: User calls requests.get(url); delegates to request('get', url, params=params, **kwargs).
Creates a temporary Session context and calls session.request(method='get', url=url, **kwargs).
Constructs a Request object from parameters, calls prepare_request() to merge with session defaults, then calls send().
Creates a PreparedRequest and populates it by calling p.prepare() with merged headers, cookies, auth, and other session settings.
Sequentially prepares the request: method, URL, headers, cookies, body, auth, and hooks, creating ready-to-send bytes.
Retrieves an HTTPAdapter via get_adapter(), applies default settings (stream, verify, cert, proxies), and calls adapter.send().
Gets or creates a connection pool, sets SSL/TLS config, calls urllib3's urlopen() to send the request, and returns build_response().
Creates a Response object from urllib3's raw response, populating status_code, headers, encoding, and extracting cookies.
Back in send(), dispatches response hook if registered, extracts cookies to session jar, handles redirects if enabled, then returns Response.

flows.name: Session-based POST with authentication and redirect handling

steps.what_happens: User calls session.post(url, data=data, auth=auth); delegates to session.request(method='post', url=url, data=data, auth=auth).
Creates Request, prepares it (merging auth with session defaults), then sends it with allow_redirects=True.
prepare_auth is called; applies auth(request) if auth is provided, allowing handlers like HTTPBasicAuth to inject credentials.
Transmits PreparedRequest and returns initial Response (e.g., 302 redirect).
Receives initial response, extracts Location header, creates new PreparedRequest for redirect URL, and recursively sends it.
Rebuilds auth, cookies, and method for the redirect (e.g., 302 converts POST to GET), persists cookies, and yields final Response.
Collects all redirect responses into history, returns final Response with history attribute populated.

flows.name: Response content access with lazy decoding

steps.what_happens: Response returned from send() has _content=False, indicating content not yet consumed.
User accesses r.content; property reads from urllib3 raw response using iter_content() in chunks, caches result in _content.
User accesses r.text; property gets content and decodes using response.encoding (or apparent_encoding if not set).
User calls r.json(); detects JSON encoding (UTF-8/16/32) using guess_json_utf() if needed, then json.loads() the content.

boundaries.note: Delegates to urllib3's PoolManager and HTTPConnectionPool for actual socket-level HTTP transmission, SSL/TLS, and connection pooling.
Checks compatibility of urllib3, chardet/charset_normalizer, and cryptography versions at import time.
HTTPAdapter is a subclass of BaseAdapter; users can subclass HTTPAdapter to customize transport behavior (connection pooling, SSL, retries).
AuthBase is a callable base class that users can subclass to implement custom authentication schemes.
Users can register response hooks (callables) in request parameters or session; dispatch_hook calls them to allow custom response processing.
Users can mount custom BaseAdapter implementations to handle specific URL schemes (e.g., custom protocol handlers).
PreparedRequest represents the boundary between user input and network transmission; all user-provided data is normalized and validated before send().

survey.testing_posture: The repository includes a comprehensive test suite in the tests/ directory with 14 test files totaling approximately 4,700+ lines. Key test modules are: test_requests.py (3,050+ lines, 246 tests covering core request/response behavior), test_lowlevel.py (428 lines, 14 tests for PreparedRequest and model internals), test_utils.py (990 lines, 76 utility function tests), test_structures.py (91 lines), test_hooks.py (22 lines), and test_adapters.py. Tests use conftest.py for pytest configuration and test fixtures (58 lines). A test server implementation in testserver/server.py (176 lines) provides a local HTTP endpoint for integration testing. The testing approach is integration-oriented, using actual HTTP servers rather than pure mocks, enabling validation of the full request/response pipeline.

Custom Sphinx theme support code for Requests documentation (Flask theme utilities).

conventions: Request objects flow through a two-stage pipeline: unprepared Request → PreparedRequest (ready to send). This separation allows merging session settings and preparing bytes without modifying the original Request.
The Session is the primary stateful object; module-level API functions (get, post, etc.) create temporary Sessions rather than maintaining module-level state, ensuring clean resource cleanup.

Hooks are callback dictionaries with event keys ('response' is currently the only event); they are registered per-request and merged with session hooks using merge_hooks(). All hooks are called via dispatch_hook().
Authentication handlers are callables (auth(request)) that take a PreparedRequest and modify it in-place to inject credentials. AuthBase.__call__ is the extension point.
Adapters are URL prefix-based routers; Session.mount(prefix, adapter) registers adapters, and get_adapter(url) returns the longest-matching prefix adapter. HTTPAdapter is the default.

Cookie handling relies on RequestsCookieJar (wrapping http.cookiejar.CookieJar) and merge_cookies(). Session persists cookies across requests; they are extracted from responses and merged into subsequent requests.
Settings merging (merge_setting) follows the pattern: request value > session value > None. For dict-type settings, both are merged and None values are stripped.

Redirect following is opt-in (allow_redirects=True) and delegated to SessionRedirectMixin.resolve_redirects(). It respects max_redirects and automatically adjusts method/body for certain status codes.

Exceptions are wrapped at the adapter boundary; urllib3 exceptions are caught and re-raised as Requests exception subclasses (ConnectionError, Timeout, ProxyError, etc.) with the original PreparedRequest attached.

Response content is lazy-loaded; r.content triggers reading from urllib3's raw response, and r.text decodes it. Encoding is determined from Content-Type header or guessed via charset_normalizer/chardet.

survey.architecture: Requests is a human-friendly HTTP client library for Python that provides a simplified interface for making HTTP requests. It abstracts over urllib3, handling connection pooling, SSL/TLS verification, cookies, authentication, redirects, and content encoding transparently. The library is organized into several layers: a public API layer (api.py) with convenience functions like `get()` and `post()`, a session management layer (sessions.py) that persists configuration across requests, a request/response model layer (models.py) representing HTTP requests and responses, and an adapter layer (adapters.py) that interfaces with urllib3 for actual network I/O.

entry_points.what_it_starts: Module-level convenience functions that users call directly to make HTTP requests; creates a Session internally and delegates to Session.request().
Session class initialization creates adapters and persistent state; Session.request() orchestrates the full request/response cycle.
Module initialization checks urllib3, chardet, and charset_normalizer compatibility at import time.

core_abstractions.role: Immutable representation of a fully-prepared HTTP request ready to be sent; contains method, url, headers, body, cookies, and hooks.
Represents an HTTP response from a server; provides lazy/streaming content access, encoding detection, JSON parsing, and context manager support.
Central orchestrator that manages cookies, authentication, proxies, and adapters; coordinates request preparation, sending, and redirect handling.
Translates PreparedRequest to urllib3 PoolManager calls; handles connection pooling, SSL/TLS verification, and HTTP semantics.

relationships.note: All module-level API functions create a Session context to execute the request.
Session.request() creates a Request object from user parameters.
Session.prepare_request() merges Request settings with session defaults and creates a PreparedRequest.
Session.send() retrieves the appropriate adapter via get_adapter() and delegates the actual send to it.
Session extends SessionRedirectMixin to inherit redirect handling logic.
HTTPAdapter.send() calls build_response() to construct a Response from urllib3's response.
Session.__init__() creates HTTPAdapter instances for http:// and https:// and mounts them via mount().
Session.send() dispatches response hooks after receiving a response from the adapter.
Session.request() calls prepare_request() to construct a PreparedRequest before sending.
PreparedRequest.prepare_auth() applies auth handler (if provided) to add authentication headers.

flows.name: Simple GET request via module API

steps.what_happens: Entry point: user calls requests.get(url). Convenience function delegates to module-level request().
request() creates a Session context manager and calls session.request('GET', url, **kwargs).
Constructs a Request object from method/url/params/data/headers/etc, then calls prepare_request().
Merges request settings with session defaults (headers, cookies, auth) and creates a PreparedRequest via p.prepare().
Orchestrates preparation: prepare_method(), prepare_url(), prepare_headers(), prepare_cookies(), prepare_body(), prepare_auth(), prepare_hooks().
Merges environment settings (proxies, verify, cert, stream) via merge_environment_settings().
Resolves proxies, gets appropriate adapter via get_adapter(url), calls adapter.send(prepared_request, **kwargs).
Gets urllib3 connection via get_connection_with_tls_context(), verifies certificate, constructs request URL, calls conn.urlopen().
Converts urllib3 response to requests.Response object with status, headers, raw content stream.
Dispatches response hooks, extracts cookies from response, handles redirect if allow_redirects=True.
Session exits, returns Response object to caller.
After receiving initial response, if allow_redirects=True and response is redirect (3xx), calls resolve_redirects().
Generator that loops: extracts Location header, copies prepared request, updates URL, modifies method/body based on status code.
Calls rebuild_auth() to remove Authorization if hostname changed, rebuild_proxies() for proxy configuration.
Extracts cookies from redirect response via extract_cookies_to_jar(), merges with session cookies.
Recursively calls self.send() with modified prepared request to follow chain of redirects.
Collects all redirect responses into history list, returns final response with history attached.

flows.name: Session with persistent state across requests

steps.what_happens: User creates a Session object: initializes headers, cookies, auth, proxies, hooks, adapters.
Mount HTTPAdapters for http:// and https:// schemes.
First request: prepare_request() merges request params with session.headers, session.cookies, session.auth.
After response, extract_cookies_to_jar() merges response cookies into session.cookies.
Second request reuses session: cookies from first request automatically included via prepare_request() merge.
User calls close() or exits context manager: closes all adapter connections.

boundaries.note: Validates urllib3 version compatibility at import time; urllib3 is the core HTTP transport dependency.
Requires either chardet or charset_normalizer for character encoding detection; warns if neither available.
HTTPAdapter delegates actual HTTP I/O to urllib3's PoolManager and HTTPConnectionPool via conn.urlopen().
Cookie handling relies on http.cookiejar.CookieJar from Python standard library.
Response.iter_content() allows custom streaming of response body; users can consume content lazily or in chunks.
AuthBase is a callable protocol; users can subclass to implement custom authentication schemes.
Hooks system allows registration of callable handlers on 'response' events; users register hooks in Request or Session.
BaseAdapter is an abstract base for protocol handlers; users can subclass to implement custom transports.
All Requests exceptions inherit from RequestException; users can catch this base exception to handle any Requests-specific error.

conventions: PreparedRequest is immutable after preparation: prepare() should be called once before sending. The request is read-only after construction.
Response content is lazy by default: accessing response.content triggers full body download; use response.iter_content() to stream.
Session is the recommended way to make multiple requests: reuses adapters, persists cookies, and manages connection pooling efficiently.
URLs are normalized via prepare_url(): parameters are URL-encoded, fragments are preserved, and IDNA encoding is applied to hostnames.
Authentication is applied last in PreparedRequest.prepare(): auth handlers receive the fully-prepared request and can modify headers.
Hooks are dispatched as generators in Session.send(): response hooks can inspect/modify the response before it's returned to the user.
Redirects are followed recursively via SessionRedirectMixin.resolve_redirects(): auth headers are stripped on cross-host redirects, method changes based on status code.
Proxies are resolved at send time via resolve_proxies() in utils.py: environment variables or explicit proxy dict can specify per-scheme proxy URLs.
CaseInsensitiveDict is used for headers: user-provided headers are merged case-insensitively with session/request defaults.
Type hints use TypeAlias and Protocol for internal types (UriType, DataType, etc.) but remain optional runtime checks for compatibility.
